# gitmoap_team_members (Data Source)

The people on a team. Only members of the team's organization can read it.

The token needs `team:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

resource "gitmoap_team" "reviewers" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
  name     = "Reviewers"
  slug     = "reviewers"
}

data "gitmoap_team_members" "example" {
  team_id = gitmoap_team.reviewers.team_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `team_id` (String) Team ID

### Read-Only

- `members` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members))

<a id="nestedatt--members"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members`

Read-Only:

- `added_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members--added_by))
- `created_at` (String)
- `expires_at` (String) When their place on the team ends. After it, the team's access no longer reaches them.
- `role` (String) A member's place on a team. Maintainers manage the roster.
- `synced_at` (String) When the identity provider last confirmed this place, for a mirrored roster.
- `team_id` (String)
- `user` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members--user))

<a id="nestedatt--members--added_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members.added_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
